title: A Dapper query and the project's own result-based error contract

consumerGuidance.architecture: This project reads through Dapper against SQL Server. EF Core is used only in Shop.Data and is not referenced here. The established error contract in Shop.Data.Dapper is QueryResult<T>, not exceptions.
consumerGuidance.notes: The query is bounded by the supplied page size and takes an existing covering index on SupplierId, ActiveFrom. No timing concern has been supplied.

forbiddenFindings.example: Requiring AsNoTracking, Include, AsSplitQuery or compiled queries in a Dapper project.
Requiring exceptions instead of QueryResult<T>, or a different result library.
Requiring a nullable return or a TryGet pattern in place of the project's QueryResult<T>.
Requiring caching, a different index or batching with no supplied measurement, when the query is already bounded and indexed.
Objecting to the raw string SQL literal's formatting or to parameter naming.

notes: Counterexample to tenant-filter-and-query-per-item: correct parameterization, tenant predicate retained, bounded page size and no supplied cost evidence, in a non-EF store.
